column1: # Closed lists that stay closed: file, name, reason class, expert way out (tab-separated).
# Reason classes: grammar, soundness, ir, kernel, protocol, fixed-standard.

column4: the nine x86-64 rflags status and control bits `jet debug`'s `registers` names when set (CF, PF, AF, ZF, SF, TF, IF, DF and OF), by X64_TRACE_FLAG_BITS' bit; fixed by the instruction set, so there is nothing for library code to extend, and a reader wanting another bit reads the raw rflags value the same row prints

the runtime words (by module storage name, each exported as the data symbol `jet_rt_<name>`) that `jet debug` writes in a stopped program around an in-process evaluation and puts back after, the one declaration both the runtime object's exports (JetIR BuildLibrary.jet) and the debugger's lookup (JetDebug NativeEval.jet native_eval_routed, in this order) read; another word is a change to that debugger-runtime protocol, landing with its value in native_eval_routed and its storage in JetRuntime, not a library extension

the musl thread functions the C startup builds the runtime's thread functions from (link_thread_create's pthread_attr_init, pthread_attr_setstacksize, pthread_create and pthread_attr_destroy, then pthread_join and pthread_detach as they are), handed to JetRuntime Thread.jet jet_rt_thread_libc in three fixed argument registers; another function is a new call in that synthesized code or a new parameter of that export, and library code starts threads through the runtime's thread_spawn instead
the sixteen x86-64 condition codes, fixed by the instruction set; there is nothing for library code to extend

the row kinds of the x86-64 emission log (JET_X64_EMIT_LOG), one per instruction form the encoder writes that can branch or touch memory (jcc, jmp, call, call through a register, memory operand, division, string copy, inline-asm template); a new form is a new variant the encoder logs, not a library extension

the sixteen x86-64 general-purpose register names by encoding number (rax through r15), as the emission log prints a row's base and index registers; fixed by the instruction set, there is nothing for library code to extend

the sixteen x86-64 condition-code mnemonics by condition number (o through g), as the emission log prints a jcc row; fixed by the instruction set like X64Cond, there is nothing for library code to extend

the ways an x86-64 instruction leaves (on to the next, a jmp, a call, a jcc, a loop or jrcxz, a return, a stop), as x64_decode reports them for the debugger's placer (NativePlace.jet native_moved rewrites a relative jmp, call and jcc and refuses a loop) and for the listings that name where a branch goes; the forms are fixed by the instruction set, so another one lands with its decoder rows, not as a library extension
the sixteen x86-64 32-bit general-register names by encoding number (eax through r15d), as objdump -M intel spells them; fixed by the instruction set, there is nothing for library code to extend
the sixteen x86-64 16-bit general-register names by encoding number (ax through r15w), as objdump -M intel spells them; fixed by the instruction set, there is nothing for library code to extend

the sixteen x86-64 byte-register names a REX prefix gives by encoding number (al through r15b), as objdump -M intel spells them; fixed by the instruction set, there is nothing for library code to extend
the four byte registers encodings 4-7 name without a REX prefix (ah, ch, dh, bh); fixed by the instruction set, there is nothing for library code to extend
the six x86-64 segment registers by encoding number (es, cs, ss, ds, fs, gs); fixed by the instruction set, there is nothing for library code to extend

the 32 comparison predicates cmpps and its kin spell into their mnemonics by immediate (eq through true_us), as objdump -M intel spells them; fixed by the instruction set, there is nothing for library code to extend

the integer comparison predicates vpcmp spells into its mnemonic by immediate (eq through nle; 3 and 7 keep their immediate), as objdump -M intel spells them; fixed by the instruction set, there is nothing for library code to extend
the four EVEX embedded rounding modes a register form names under EVEX.b (rn, rd, ru, rz with sae); fixed by the instruction set, there is nothing for library code to extend

the runtime's fiber context switch, the one template whose saved-register layout every switch site shares so any site resumes any other, assembled only to X64_FIBER_SWITCH_BYTES and only for the runtime library that defines the fiber entry; another rail is a new constant with its fixed bytes and its arm in x64_assemble_template, and library code switches fibers through the runtime's scheduler instead

the whole body of a signal restorer: rt_sigreturn (syscall 15) on the stack the handler returned to, fixed by the Linux x86-64 signal frame ABI and assembled only to X64_SIGNAL_RETURN_BYTES for the runtime library; there is nothing for library code to extend, and code installs handlers through the runtime's signal routes instead

the child side of the runtime's clone rail: the new thread tests the clone result, pops its entry and argument, aligns its stack, calls the entry and exits, assembled only to X64_CLONE_CHILD_BYTES after the audited clone prologue and only for the runtime library; another rail is a new constant with its fixed bytes and its arm in x64_assemble_template, and library code starts threads through the runtime's thread_spawn instead

the four timeline lanes of a `jet.canvas.profile` document (spans, zones, waits, io), in the order the Canvas profile view draws them and Docs/Spec/Reference/canvas-protocol.md names them; another lane is a protocol schema change that lands with the view, not a library extension

the paths a Canvas listener serves under its session secret (page, panel page, app, session, project, graph, source, transaction, debug, profile, status, version), each one the Canvas page requests by name, plus Unbuilt for a Canvas path whose handler this host lacks and Unknown for any other; another route is a page and host change that lands together, not a library extension

the entry-based `jet audit` subcommands (copies, foreign, writes), each a command word the CLI parses into its own report plan; another subject is a new `jet audit` subcommand with its plan and report, not a library extension

the exact field set of an accepted generation's audit record in the `jet.budget-manifest` schema; another field is a new manifest schema version that the store writes and reads together, not a library extension

the budget report measurement fields a prior baseline generation must share with the candidate to be compared with it; another field changes which stored reports compare, so it lands with a budget report schema version
the budget report subject fields (target triple, target class, profile) a prior baseline generation must share with the candidate; another field lands with a budget report schema version

the three ways `jet budget update` accepts a report, each written as the audit `kind` (`pass`, `bootstrap`, `exception`) the manifest reader checks; another way is a new audit kind in the manifest schema

the three states the baseline staleness rule gives a budget's newest compatible generation (none, fresh, stale), which decide whether a bootstrap may replace it; another state is a change to that rule, not a library extension

the four kinds of node the `jet build` scheduler runs (a step, a target's image, a checked library, a target built for the machine running the build), each with its own arm that starts and finishes it; another kind is a new Build call with its scheduler arm, not a library extension, and library code adds work to a build as a `b.run` step

the three ends a task the `jet build` run loop (jet_cli_build_run_nodes) starts hands back on its channel (the steps it ran, a target node's output and wall time, the panic text of a task that stopped), each with its own arm in the loop that records it or stops the build; another end is a new kind of task the loop starts, with its arm, not a library extension, and library code adds work to a build as a `b.run` step

the four places a compiler control's value comes from (default, settings, environment variable, command-line flag), in the precedence order `jet env vars` reports as its `source`; another place is a new layer in the control resolver and in the `env.vars` status schema, not a library extension

the Core packages the toolchain's Core library leaves for each program to lower, those fewer than one in a hundred of the program files under Examples/ and the gauntlet's entries name; Tests/Guards/core_shipped.jet recounts that share and fails naming the package that crossed it, so a package moves in or out with the census, not as a library extension

the three edit sets `jet fix` writes besides `--markers` (the checker's suggestions, the `--style` moves, the `--pin-failures` contracts), each a command-line flag the CLI parses into its own arm of the fix run; another set is a new `jet fix` flag with its arm and its recheck, not a library extension

the three ends of the native route (the linked executable, the link inputs a package's link step links in place of Jet's own link, a failure), each with its own arm in jet_cli_build_native that writes the image, runs the link step (LinkStep.jet) or reports; another end is a new stage of the native route with its arm, not a library extension

the eight kinds of automatic choice `jet inspect choices` reports (storage form, inlining, collection, copies, placement, exposure, rights, context), in the order the text report lists them and the `inspect.choices` status record writes as its `kinds` field, each read from its own compiler fact (sema's reactive upgrade, promotion, copy, web partition, route marker, server-only marker and context read facts, JetIR's inlining log); another kind is a new compiler fact with its rows in that report and status schema, not a library extension

the five outcomes of one key in bare `jet`'s command picker (keep going, quit, enter or leave the alternate-screen reference, submit a command line), each with its own arm in the picker's session loop that draws, switches screens or ends the session; another outcome is a new session step with its arm, not a library extension

the keys the picker decodes from a terminal's input bytes (a typed character, Enter, Alt+Enter, Escape, Tab, Backspace, the four arrows, F1, the quit keys and any other key), the ECMA-48 and xterm sequences its reference binds; another key is a new binding decoded from its sequence and handled in every view, not a library extension

the four views of bare `jet`'s command picker (the categorized palette, search results, one command's detail, the two-pane reference), each with its own renderer and key handling; another view is a new screen of the picker with its renderer and keys, not a library extension

the three folders of a toolchain tree the `jet-source/v1` source key hashes (Compiler, Core, Jetpack), the files a compiler is built from and so the key Compiler/build.jet names a built compiler by and `b.jet_built_from` compares; another folder changes what every key names, a new key version that the build file and the compiler's runtime pack change with, not a library extension

the inherent method names of a routed Core module's types that the compiler looks up by a string literal (an interpolation's `to_string`, a handle route's `cross`), so a lazily loaded type keeps them; Compiler/JetDriver/Tests/CoreReach.jet holds the list to exactly the names the compiler's sources spell for those types, so a new literal lookup lands in the compiler with its name here, not as a library extension

the top-level functions of Core modules that aren't routed which the compiler calls by a name it spells as a string literal right after the module's name (a `Matrix * Matrix` product's core.compute `matmul`), so the reach keeps them when no program spells them; Compiler/JetDriver/Tests/CoreReach.jet holds the list to exactly the names the compiler's sources spell that way, so a new call by name lands in the compiler with its name here, not as a library extension

the runtime unit's own lock, wait, park and yield functions (sync_mutex_lock, sync_thread_lock, sync_sole_enter, sync_wait, sync_futex_wait, sync_cond_wait, sync_park, scheduler_yield), local symbols no export names and so no generated vocabulary holds, that `jet debug` traps while an evaluation runs as the backstop for every lock or wait a path reaches without its export (native_eval_locks); another primitive is a change to JetRuntime's synchronization that lands with its name here, not a library extension

the runtime routines that a breakpoint condition's code, placed in the program, may reach but must not run there: the runtime's stops (a numeric failure, a shift past the width, an unreachable point, a sequence's capacity overflow), which report and end a task, and the allocator's paths for a request the condition's arena doesn't serve (a large block, a context allocator's handler), which would allocate from the program's heap. Each call of one goes to the trampoline's stub, which hands the hit to the debugger (native_place_routed). Three are the runtime unit's local symbols, which no export or generated vocabulary names. A routine missing here would run in the program from a hit whose condition the program can see, so another stop or allocator slow path lands with its runtime body and its row here, not as a library extension
the artifact file kinds Jet writes, each paired with its fixed extension in ARTIFACT_KINDS; another kind is a new artifact format with its own extension and reader, not a library extension
the token classes the highlight generator assigns every grammar token for the editor grammars it writes; another class is a change to the generated grammars, not a library extension
the binary operators the grammar parses; a new operator is a language change through the syntax registry, and library code names an operation as a function instead

the argument forms an interpolation selector's parentheses hold (an Int literal, a quoted text, a `:Unit` style word, or an expression computed after the value), each a parse the formatter prints back; a selector's meaning is open, its trait `NameFormat`, but another argument form is a change to the interpolation grammar, not a library extension

the forms of the structured `task` surface the grammar parses (`task { … }`, `task.timeout(d)` and the `task.all`, `task.race` and `task.any` combinators), each lowered by task_form_call and read back by the parser, formatter and sema through task_form_of; another form is a language change through the syntax registry and the spec's structured-task rules, and library code builds its own waiting on core.tasks' receivers (`after`, `waitall`, `waitany`) instead
the prefix operators the grammar parses (`-`, `!` and the complement `~`); a new one is a language change through the syntax registry, and library code names an operation as a function instead

the three events a build tells the `jet debug --build` console (a compile-time batch loaded into the child, a call into the child starting, a marker body reaching a line a breakpoint waits on), each answered by its own arm of JetDebug NativeBuild.jet's receive; another event is a change to that build-to-debugger protocol that lands with its arm there, not a library extension

the x86-64 ALU opcode group (add, or, adc, sbb, and, sub, xor, cmp) by its /digit in the 0x81 and 0x83 encodings, fixed by the instruction set; JetBackend's encoder group X64Alu is a checked subset of it, and there is nothing for library code to extend

the mnemonics the compiler's x86-64 template assembler (JetBackend X64/InlineAsm.jet) encodes through its line grammar, which sema checks every `#FFI(asm)` body against (E3221) and the assembler refuses any other first word by; JetBackend's encoder group X64Shift is a checked subset of it; another mnemonic is a new encoding in that assembler with its row here, not a library extension

the further mnemonics only the runtime's closed templates spell (the fiber switch, GS base, signal return and clone child rails), each template assembled whole to its fixed bytes; another word comes with a new rail constant and its bytes in X64/InlineAsm.jet, and library code reaches those operations through the runtime instead

the four folders Cargo finds beside a `Cargo.toml` by their default names (src, benches, examples, tests), fixed by Cargo's layout and kept lowercase by the path-case lint; there is nothing for library code to extend, and a crate naming other folders lists them in its own manifest

the folder classes the acronym path-case lint (Jet.AcronymPathCase) keeps by what a tree holds rather than where it sits, each with its rule in PathCase.jet; another class is a change to that lint's rule, landing with its rule and its UI snapshot, and a tree outside every class follows the TitleCase rule

the compiler hooks of the Prelude markers, each a projection the parser writes into a typed AST field or a check sema runs, keyed by the Prelude declaration it belongs to; a package marker reaches no hook (it is an ordinary marker), so another member is new compiler behavior for a Jet-owned marker, not a library extension

the ways a `jet` flag is written on the command line (bare, bare or `=false`, one value, bare or one value, one value per repeat), each with its own arm where a remembered setting writes the flag's words; another way is a change to the command-line grammar, not a library extension

the compiler's closed machine-effect type, one case per machine root of Compiler/Prelude/Effects.jet in its order, which EFFECT_ROOT_COUNT checks against the roots while the compiler builds (E3010 on any difference); a new machine effect lands in Effects.jet with its runtime enforcement and its case here, and library code declares a service effect over the machine roots in Core/Effects/Effects.jet instead

the three promises a Jet environment variable carries (User: a stable setting; Maintainer: a support and diagnosis switch; Internal: Jet-owned state handed to a child process, with no compatibility promise), one generated table each on Docs/Spec/Reference/environment.md; another section is a new promise class with its own table, not a library extension

the four kinds of row in the public metadata contract (fact, operation, phase, failure), the classes #3520's versioned model publishes and Tests/MetadataContract.jet checks every row against; another kind is a new version of that contract on #3520, not a library extension

the four surfaces of the public metadata contract (preparation, reflection, publishing, advanced program control), the parts #3520's versioned model is cut into and Tests/MetadataContract.jet checks every row against; another surface is a new version of that contract on #3520, not a library extension

the kinds of contract an impl of a compiler-owned trait is checked against (fixed methods, an operator hook, a codec verb, a literal source, a conversion hook, a checked-text checker, a structural derive), each a check sema runs and a lowering JetIR applies; Tools/Agent/OwnedTraitRows.jet reads which one a trait carries from its Prelude declaration, so another trait is a declaration in Compiler/Prelude/Traits.jet and another kind is new compiler behavior, not a library extension

the ways a compiler-owned trait's method takes its receiver (no receiver, `self` with any access, `self` with one fixed access), which the impl contract check compares an impl's method against; Tools/Agent/OwnedTraitRows.jet reads it from the method's header in Compiler/Prelude/Traits.jet, so another way is a new receiver form of the language, not a library extension

the hardware and software counters the `memory` lens of `jet perf run` samples (L1D, LLC and dTLB read misses, page faults), in the order the runtime opens them and writes their periods and errnos (JetRuntime PerfSamples.jet perf_counter_config and perf_counters_start) and a record's kind names them, each with its row field in TraceProfileRow; another counter is a new perf_event_open configuration in the runtime, a new record kind and a new row field that land together, not a library extension

the IRModule.constant_rows key prefixes of the writable cells a function builds (module storage from BuildStatic.jet ir_storage_address, a memoized function's store from BuildMemo.jet ir_memo_cell, a Shared site from BuildSharedSites.jet ir_shared_site_word), each exported from the prebuilt Core library as a `jet_core_cell_` data symbol; another prefix is a new kind of IR-built writable cell that lands with its address builder and its row here, not as a library extension

where the stops receipt (ir_stop_exports) traces a called code word back to in a library's IR: a function's address, the word at offset 0 of a rail cell, a parameter of the function, or anything else; each is a kind of IR operand the trace reads, so another kind lands with the IR op that makes it and its arm in ir_code_sources, not as a library extension

the runtime functions that end the process instead of publishing a stop the calling program takes (allocation failure, the checked heap's misuse report, a capacity overflow of a sequence, a text or an owner count, an invalid box layout, an internal defect), through which the stops receipt (ir_stop_exports) traces no stop; listing a function that can return a stop to its caller would drop the poll after a call that needs one, so a new fatal route lands with its runtime body and its row here, not as a library extension

the runtime functions that run a program's memory hooks (a context allocator's handler and its release, the checked heap's allocation observers, a value's clone and drop glue, a context value's release, an error payload's release), whose stop the program takes at its next stop check, so the stops receipt (ir_stop_exports) traces no stop through them and allocation, freeing, cloning and dropping take no poll after them; a hook whose stop must be taken at its call site does not belong here, so a new memory hook lands with its runtime body and its row here, not as a library extension

the runtime files whose every function the debugger's eval runtime replaces with a stub (the allocator and its large-block cache, retain and release, the journey and its thread-local half), because their code as built would change the stopped program's heap, owner counts or journey from inside the eval fork; a file missing here lets an eval run the program's own allocator state, so a new runtime file of that kind lands with its stub in the eval runtime and its row here, not as a library extension, and library code allocates and counts through these files without naming them

the runtime functions the debugger's eval runtime replaces by name (the Shared cell's lock and its release, the scheduler's task context, cleanup shield and stop propagation), each of which would wait on another thread or read scheduler state the eval fork does not have; a function missing here can hang an eval until the debugger's budget ends, so a new runtime lock or scheduler hook lands with its stub row here, not as a library extension, and library code locks through Shared without naming these

the runtime files of the stop report (the trap and its message tables), whose `_stop` and `_exit` functions and report header (`trap_header`) start a report the eval fork ends at with its own stub (ir_eval_stop_root), so the eval link follows no call past them; a file missing here would count a stop's report path as code the fork runs and refuse evals that can only stop, so a new stop-report file lands with its row here, not as a library extension

the places a value's layout keeps the selector of its variant (its own word, word 0 of its box, or its box pointer's nullness), one per variant layout the IR builder lays out, each described by its own DWARF discriminant in ir_x64_debug_variants; a new variant layout lands with its arm there, not as a library extension
the IR instruction set every backend lowers; library code reaches new behavior through Core calls and runtime routes, and a new op lands with its lowering in every backend

the share keys the IR builder emits as the clone of a counted value (a box, a trait value, a function value), each lowered by every backend as a retain; a new counted kind lands with its clone lowering and its row here, not as a library extension
the optimizer passes `--opt-disable` can name, one per pass the IR optimizer runs; a new pass lands with its row here and its skip check in the pass loop, not as a library extension

the kinds of module data row a function's x86-64 selection can name before the module tables exist (a text, a String header of an IR data row, a static Int, the FMA probe byte), each replayed into IRX64Tables by its own arm in ir_x64_tables_add; another kind is a new data row the selector emits, which lands with its arm there, not a library extension

the three places a completion can stand as the member-access grammar reads the tokens before it (no `.` ending at the cursor's word, a `.` written right after a receiver word, a `.` after anything else), each with its own answer in lsp_completion_response (every name in scope, the receiver type's members, nothing); another place is a new member-access form in the grammar that lands with its answer there, not a library extension

the semantic-token legend `initialize` announces; a token's type travels as its index here (LSP_TOKEN_* in Tokens.jet), so another type is a new LSP_TOKEN_* constant and legend entry the client reads together, not a library extension

the semantic-token modifier legend `initialize` announces (declaration, readonly, modification, macro); a token's modifiers travel as bits by index here (LSP_MODIFIER_* in Tokens.jet), so another modifier is a new LSP_MODIFIER_* bit and legend entry the client reads together, not a library extension

the exceptions of the impl placement style rule (#6561 rules c, d, e, f and g: a protocol side, a `#Target` impl, a derive-written impl, an impl whose head carries an error of the same check, an inherent impl with its own markers; #6281 c159 rule h: a conditional impl, whose head bounds its type's parameters), each an impl form, marker or head error the grammar gives that the type's body cannot hold as written, with its own arm in parser_impl_placement_rule, which `jet check --style`, `jet fix --style` and the impl placement guard share; another exception is a change to that rule on #6561, not a library extension

the body passes sema_finalize_pass_modules runs (Modules, whole modules; Core, the bodies a Core demand wave names; Codec, the codecs a codec wave fills; Derive, the derived methods a derive wave demands), each a checker pass with its own scheduling and its own way of appending to a module's result; another kind is a new checker pass that lands with its wave driver, not a library extension

the stages a body stream module passes through in sema_check_body_stream's scheduler (Waiting, admitted but not yet claimed for its preparation; Preparing, a thread builds its post-summary scope; Rescan, its preparation wanted a host callback and the lead prepares it again; Open, its jobs can be claimed), each a state the scheduler's one lock moves a module through; another stage is a scheduler change, not a library extension

the steps a body stream thread takes next (Body, check a claimed job; Prep, prepare a stream module; Await, the lead waits for the jobs of the module it checks next; Stop), each a branch of the stream's thread and lead loops; another step is a scheduler change, not a library extension

the Core records a rule batch's generated check builds each heard call from (CompilerCall, CompilerName, CompilerArg, SourceSpan), whose literals only that check may write (SemaCheckContext.compiler_records) and which sema fills from the batch's own word and text columns; another record is a change to the CompilerCall shape in Core/Compiler that lands here and in sema_call_rule_batch_expression together, not a library extension

the core.math members with an F32-width source of their own that sema routes F32 calls to (sema_call_core_math_f32_own and sema_call_core_math_f32_kept); it restates which core.math functions declare an F32 form, so it should become a view derived from core.math's declarations, and until then a new F32 source lands with its row here

the finalization points sema_local_splice_owners lands body comptime values at (Finalized, a finalized result carrying the whole-program stamps; Unstamped, a finalization's checked bodies after its Core demand; Undemanded, its body half before that demand), each a point in sema_finalize_graph's own pass order that decides whether the bodies carry stamps (sema_local_splice_stamped) and whether the Core demand already ran over them (sema_local_splice_demanded); another point is a new finalization stage that lands with its driver landing, not a library extension

the context fields whose meaning a Core module carries (`context.logger` and `context.on_stop` as its keys, `context.trace` through its reader), each mapped by sema_context_field_module to the module the loader loads wherever the field is spelled; another field is a language change to the implicit context (spec.md), and a library adds a value as its own `#ContextKey` instead

the language's own context field names (`context.allocator` through `context.trace`) and `get`, the one `context` method, which a `#ContextKey` constant may not take because `context.<name>` already means them; another field is a language change to the implicit context (spec.md, Deadlines and teaching diagnostics), and a library adds a value as its own `#ContextKey` instead

the `core.mem` operations spec.md (Unsafe and low-level memory) names E3101 outside `#Unsafe` (volatile_read, volatile_write, copy, fill, alloc_raw, free_raw, window), each refused at its call before its arguments are checked, and left out of the effect pass's E3103 call check so the call reports once; another operation is a spec change that names it E3101, not a library extension, and library code marks its own function `#Unsafe("reason")`, which E3103 gates instead

the error types the compiler owns and no Core source declares, each a failure domain sema admits where no declaration answers: the build and comptime host values BuildError, CompilerError and CompilerPackageError, the runtime handles Closed, FieldError, IOError, RangeError, TextError and UTF8Error, and the Expired record; a #run check holds each to its registry and keeps it out of Core.rows error_types; another member comes with the registry row that types it, and a library error type is declared `#Error` in its Core module, which Core.rows error_types lists instead

the precise number types (Decimal, Fraction and Complex) whose checked operations sema runs through their core.math functions by role; it restates core.math's own types, so it should become a view derived from their role rows, and until then a new precise type lands with its row here and its core.math functions

the carriers the checker types itself that a program may write bare and no Core source or registry row declares: the raw pointer Ptr, the geometry coordinate spaces (Camera, Device, Screen, World, View) a point, delta or transform names, the compute shapes Vec and Matrix, the collection windows View and ViewMut, a generator's Stream, a file reader's FileLines, and the DataGroupedQuery a query's group_by yields, which core.data declares without exporting; another carrier comes with the checker rules that type it, and a library type is declared in its Core module and reached through that module's export instead

the outside debuggers and profilers (lldb, gdb, Linux perf, go's pprof and otelcol) a Debug or Perf case runs without, so the case proves what jet debug and jet perf do alone; the kit leaves each out of the case's PATH and refuses a case that requires one, which belongs in Tests/Cases/ToolInterop; another tool is a change to that jet-alone rule for those suites, not a library extension

the host names a case's `requires: os:`, `os-name:` and `arch:` lines and `when os`, `os-name` and `arch` conditions may write, each after its kind (the unix and windows families; Linux, macOS, Windows, Android, iOS and the three BSDs; x86_64, aarch64 and x86), as core.sys and kit_steps_host_name and kit_steps_host_arch spell the host the case runs on; the kit refuses any other name rather than skip the case on every host. It is not derived: JetTestKit depends on Core alone, so Compiler/test.jet runs it without building the compiler's packages, and the one host list there, JetFoundation's TTargetOS, names the OSes jet builds for (with web, Wasm and freestanding), not families, architectures or core.sys's names. Another host is one the kit runs cases on, landing with this row, not a library extension

the C and Rust text that marks a quoted string as foreign code for the one-shot ^ mark migration; the migration runs on frozen pre-cutover text, so there is nothing to extend, and a new spelling change gets its own migration
